transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My family and our accountant insisted I come in for an evaluation, so that's the only reason I'm here. But to be honest, I’m absolutely certain I’m seeing things more clearly than everyone else and that my ideas can’t be wrong, even when my family says they make no sense.

Have there been times when you felt unusually high or energized for days, needed much less sleep, and became more talkative or active than usual? Or have these beliefs stayed the same even without any change in your mood or energy?

Yes, for most of the past year I've been incredibly energized, talking fast, working constantly, and sleeping only about three hours a night. But these beliefs and the voice don't just happen when I'm revved up; even a few months ago when my energy dipped and I slowed down, I still heard that voice at night and stayed convinced the co-op was tracking my drones.

When your mood and energy returned completely to normal, did the voice and your belief that the co-op was tracking your drones continue for at least 2 weeks? Or do they only happen during times when you’re unusually energized or depressed?

Yes, they absolutely continued for well over two weeks. Even during that spell a few months back when my energy leveled out and I wasn't rushing around the farm, I still heard that man's voice at night and remained convinced the co-op was tracking my drones.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F31.2, F20.0]. The interview now establishes a prolonged period of elevated energy, decreased need for sleep, pressured/fast speech, and increased activity consistent with a manic syndrome, while the psychotic symptoms also persisted for well over 2 weeks during a period when mood/energy had returned to normal. This makes a pure mood disorder with psychotic symptoms less likely because the psychosis is not confined to mood episodes, and it makes a primary schizophrenia-spectrum disorder less likely because there is also a prominent manic syndrome. Therefore the current candidate is [F25.0].

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a prolonged manic syndrome with decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured/fast speech, and overactivity, together with persistent psychotic symptoms. Crucially, auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusional beliefs continued for well over 2 weeks during a period when mood/energy were no longer elevated, supporting schizoaffective disorder, manic type rather than a primary bipolar manic episode with psychotic features.
